To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amounts of dispersed weathering material in Frasnian limestones are controlled by the third-order eustatic cycles, the Frasnian and Famennian sea level fluctuations were controlled by the combination of glacio- and tectonoeusstasy and that the Frasnian platform was drowned by the Famennian transgression.

the Frasnian platform of the Czech Republic, as a typical example of the world-wide Frasnian carbonate platforms, was subject to strong sea-level oscillations and the F/F transition was marked by rapid rise of sea level and a very high stand of sea level.
the amount of weathering products trapped in pure carbonates is controlled by eustatic sea-level fluctuations and that this proxy is a useful tool for the reconstruction of sea-level changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of sedimentological analysis and the interpretation of the results.
the sedimentation of carbonate platforms and ramps in a time span from the Late Frasnian to the Early Famennian.
the sedimentological and geochemical aspects of carbonate platforms in the context of eustatic and palaeoclimentary changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Late Frasnian sea level was high but not highstand, the F/F transition was a rapid fall of sea level and early Famennia was a time of very low sea level.
the eustatic sea-level fluctuations in Frasnian and early Famennians times were controlled by glacioeustasy and tectonoeusstasy.

the Late Frasnian sea level was very high, the Early Famennian sea level was low, the Late Frasnarian/Famennian transition was extremely variable, and the Late Famennian sea-level rise was moderate, although the data from the Eastern Moravian platform are not conclusive enough for a more detailed analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eustatic sea-level fluctuations were superimposed on the tectonically subsiding platform and the F/F transition brought a strong change in the palaeogeography of the area.
the eustatic control of sea level is a dominant factor in carbonate sedimentation, although it is not always easy to separate it from other controls.
the Late Devonian was characterised by a very high sea level which was not stable, but oscillated rapidly and frequently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Frasnian and F/F carbonate successions are not only a result of eustasy and tectonics but also of climate.

, in the absence of tectonics and glaciation, sea-level changes are controlled by changes in climate and the weathering of continental areas, and that the amount of dispersed material is an indicator of climate change and the degree of continental weathering.
, although the Frasnian sea level was very low, it was still higher than the Famennian one.
